candidates.title: Measuring and Estimating the Bioconcentration Factor of Chemicals in Fish (Veith, DeFoe & Bergstedt 1979, J. Fish. Res. Board Can. 36(9):1040-1048)
candidates.basis: Abstract (Crossref record) gives log BCF = 0.85 log P - 0.70 for organic chemicals in fathead minnows; slope 0.85 lies inside [0.7, 1.0]. The abstract does not restrict to neutral chemicals or state the log Kow range.

candidates.title: An Evaluation of Using Partition Coefficients and Water Solubility to Estimate Bioconcentration Factors for Organic Chemicals in Fish (Veith, Macek, Petrocelli & Carroll 1980, ASTM STP 707:116-129)
candidates.basis: ASTM abstract (read through a WebSearch excerpt) gives log BCF = 0.76 log P - 0.23 for fish; slope 0.76 inside the band. Sample size is reported inconsistently (28 new chemicals in the abstract; 84 in secondary sources).

candidates.title: Correlation of bioconcentration factors (Mackay 1982, Environ. Sci. Technol. 16(5):274-278)
candidates.basis: Secondary sources (PMC9692598; WebSearch excerpts) give log BCF = log Kow - 1.32 (BCF = 0.048 Kow) for fish, r2 = 0.95. The slope is fixed at 1.0 rather than estimated freely, and sits on the band's inclusive upper edge. Crossref has no abstract; primary text not read.

candidates.title: Estimating bioconcentration factors from octanol-water partition coefficient and aqueous solubility (Isnard & Lambert 1988, Chemosphere 17(1):21-34)
candidates.basis: PMC9692598 lists log BCF = 0.80 log Kow - 0.52 (n = 107, R2 = 0.81) among equations citing this paper. The equation-to-reference mapping is by elimination, not stated explicitly. Slope 0.80 is inside the band; primary text not read.

candidates.title: Improved method for estimating bioconcentration/bioaccumulation factor from octanol/water partition coefficient (Meylan et al. 1999, Environ. Toxicol. Chem. 18(4):664-672) [METHOD DATA SET, fallback (c): BCFBAF/BCFWIN training set]
candidates.basis: Abstract (Crossref) confirms a separate nonionic equation for log Kow 1.0-7.0 over 694 chemicals (r2 = 0.73). ECETOC 2000 and an ECHA dossier (via WebSearch) give it as log BCF = 0.77 log Kow - 0.70 + sum of Fi; slope 0.77 is inside the band. The later BCFWIN v2.15 software uses 0.6598 log Kow - 0.333, which falls below the band.

candidates.title: A review of bioconcentration factor (BCF) and bioaccumulation factor (BAF) assessments for organic chemicals in aquatic organisms (Arnot & Gobas 2006, Environ. Rev. 14(4):257-297) [METHOD DATA SET, primary choice (a)]
candidates.basis: Data-set source: 5317 BCF values for 842 chemicals in 219 species (Crossref abstract). Citing papers and WebSearch excerpts of the full text report a fish fit of log BCF = 0.60 log Kow - 0.23 (r2 about 0.52, acceptable data, log Kow > 0 up to about 8.7). That slope falls below the band, but the fit is not restricted to log Kow 1-6. The regression table was not read: SFU PDF unreachable, publisher HTTP 403.

candidates.title: OPERA models for predicting physicochemical properties and environmental fate endpoints (Mansouri, Grulke, Judson & Williams 2018, J. Cheminform. 10:10) [METHOD DATA SET, fallback (b): OPERA BCF and LogP sets]
candidates.basis: Data-set source; no log BCF-log Kow slope is reported. Full text (Europe PMC PMC5843579): BCF set from PHYSPROP file EPI_BCF_Data_SDF.sdf, 685 to 618 top-quality to 608 QSAR-ready chemicals. LogP set: 15,806 to 14,544 to 14,041. Data at github.com/kmansouri/OPERA. The BCF set descends from the EPI Suite BCF data, so fallbacks (b) and (c) share lineage.

candidates.title: Nonlinear Dependence of Fish Bioconcentration on n-Octanol/Water Partition Coefficient (Bintein, Devillers & Karcher 1993, SAR QSAR Environ. Res. 1(1):29-39)
candidates.basis: Bilinear model, log BCF = 0.910 log P - 1.975 log(6.8e-7 P + 1) - 0.786 (n = 154, r = 0.950), taken from a WebSearch excerpt of the PubMed abstract. Its linear-limb coefficient 0.91 is not a straight-line OLS slope; the curve peaks near log Kow 6.

candidates.title: Comparison of BCF models based on log P (Devillers, Bintein & Domine 1996, Chemosphere 33(6):1047-1065)
candidates.basis: Comparison of linear, quadratic, polynomial and bilinear log P-based fish BCF models. Secondary sources say the linear models give similar predictions for log Kow < 6. A review, not a new slope estimate.

candidates.title: Partition coefficient to measure bioconcentration potential of organic chemicals in fish (Neely, Branson & Blau 1974, Environ. Sci. Technol. 8:1113-1115)
candidates.basis: Earliest fish log BCF-log Kow regression; PMC9692598 lists log BCF = 0.542 log Kow + 0.124 (n = 8, R2 = 0.90). The slope falls below the band.

candidates.title: Correlation of bioconcentration factors of chemicals in aquatic and terrestrial organisms with their physical and chemical properties (Kenaga 1980, Environ. Sci. Technol.)
